ShortDescription.Value: Responding emergency vehicles stop despawning in traffic jams, re-route around congestion, and get green lights along their route.

Publish.LongDescription:
Vanilla Cities Skylines II deletes a responding fire engine, ambulance or police car outright once it is flagged as stuck in traffic, and never re-evaluates its route after dispatch. This mod keeps responding units alive, re-routes them around congestion, and clears the traffic lights ahead of them — all through the game's own pathfinding and signal priority.
WHAT IT DOES
- Stuck responders stop despawning. A unit the game has flagged as stuck looks for a new route instead of being deleted in the middle of a call.
- Re-routing around congestion. Vanilla plans the route once, at dispatch, and never looks again. A responder that has been sitting in a jam asks for a fresh route that accounts for the traffic actually there now.
- Green lights along the route. Traffic lights ahead of a responding vehicle turn green as it approaches and stay green until it has passed, so the queue in front of it can clear out of the way.
The green lights are not for the ambulance. Emergency vehicles already drive through red lights in this game — what stops them is the queue of ordinary cars in front, and that queue does wait at the red. Giving it somewhere to go is what actually gets the responder moving.
This works through the game's own signal priority, at the same priority the game already grants emergency vehicles. Lights still change through their normal clearance phases, so cross traffic gets its amber and pedestrian crossings behave as usual. No light is ever forced, and every junction returns to its normal cycle by itself once the responder is through.
Every feature has its own toggle, and with the master switch off the mod is exactly vanilla. Safe to add to or remove from an existing city at any time — nothing is written into your save.
Source (open source, MIT): https://github.com/AmicusDeus/EmergencyPriority
Localized into 11 languages (German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese-BR, Russian, Chinese Simplified & Traditional). Translations are machine-generated — corrections welcome.
Made with Claude Code's Opus 5, Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 models.
Publish.ChangeLog:
v1.07 - Traffic lights now clear the way for responding vehicles
NEW: traffic lights along a responding vehicle's route turn green as it approaches, and stay green until it has passed.
The point is not the ambulance itself. Emergency vehicles already drive straight through red lights in this game — what actually stops them is the queue of ordinary cars in front, and that queue does wait at the red. This gives the queue somewhere to go, so it drains out of the way instead of pinning the responder behind it.
The game has everything needed for this already and simply never asks. It only signals ahead as far as a vehicle's braking distance reaches, and that is close to nothing once the vehicle has stopped moving — so a responder stuck in a queue, the exact case where it matters most, asks for nothing at all. This mod asks on its behalf, out to a distance you choose.
It works through the game's own signal priority, at the same priority the game already grants emergency vehicles. Lights still change through their normal clearance phases, so cross traffic gets its amber and pedestrian crossings behave as usual. No light is ever forced green, and each junction returns to its normal cycle by itself the moment the responder is through — nothing is left altered in your save, and removing the mod changes nothing back.
Two new settings, under Traffic lights: turn the feature on or off, and set how far ahead of a responder the lights react (40-300 m, default 120 m).
